evidence.claim: Construction began in 1816, then stopped when a new survey placed the site in Canada.
evidence.quote: When a new survey discovered that the 45th parallel was actually located some 0.75 miles (1.21 km) south compared to the markers on the 1771-1773 Collins–Valentine line, effectively placing the fort in Canada, all construction on this first fort stopped

evidence.claim: Local people carried away materials for homes and public buildings, and the abandoned works became known as Fort Blunder.
evidence.quote: Much of its material was scavenged by the locals for use in their own homes and public buildings. It became popularly known as "Fort Blunder" for this reason.

evidence.claim: The Webster–Ashburton Treaty moved Island Point into the United States in 1842.
evidence.quote: the Webster–Ashburton Treaty of 1842 ceded strategically important Island Point, the site of the 1816 fort and the northernmost point on Lake Champlain, to the United States.

evidence.claim: Work on a second fort, Fort Montgomery, began in 1844.

flags: NYSDOT’s 84 miles differs from catalog geometry’s 88.5; retained the official figure. Sources describe a rural corridor but give no supported driving time, detailed terrain or original road-construction campaign.
NYSDOT uses Saint Lawrence Seaway in its military-history description. Used waterways/corridor language to avoid implying that the modern Seaway existed during colonial troop movements.

Fort Blunder and Fort Montgomery were different structures on the same site. Rouses Point article conflates their names and gives an implausible 1816 date for a reused-stone house; used the detailed fort article and omitted the house.
Fort ruins are privately owned; cache does not establish authorized public access. No invitation to enter or practical access claim included.

All substantive current claims have cache support; none dropped solely for lack of evidence. Replaced generic near-border language with supported route geography. Current has no motifs; story array initialized empty.
